From the FAQ ( I think it's in the rulebook somewhere too now )

"A "hand strike" is any non-ranged, non-weapon strike that deals damage
based
on the striking minion's strength, or any minion's non-ranged damage-dealing
innate strike. "

Stutter Step is not ranged, is not a weapon strike & deals damage based on
the striking minion's strength. This qualifies it as a hand strike.

> I just see the card identifying it's strike as a Dodge, but also
> delivering strength damage. Therefore, I see it only as a Special
> Dodge, but a Dodge none the less.

I think that is the intention but because of IG's card text & the definition
of a "hand strike" SS had to be errataed.

> I understand it was errata'ed by LSJ so it can not be used in an IG
> combat, but have not really understood the need.

Very much a matter of semantics, some ppl reasonably interperet wording in
different ways to others.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Ramsteiner wrote:
> I am curious. How does it meet the criteria of a Hand Strike?
>
> I just see the card identifying it's strike as a Dodge, but also
> delivering strength damage. Therefore, I see it only as a Special
> Dodge, but a Dodge none the less.

There is nothing in the defition of a hand strike that precludes a dodge.

1) Is Stutter-Step non-ranged? Yes.
2) Is Stutter-Step a weapon-based strike? No.
3) Does Stutter-Step inflict damage based on the striking minion's
strength? Yes.

Therefore Stutter-Step is a hand strike and, barring errata to the
contrary, would be playable under Immortal Grapple.
